subject: Business
title: Central Bank Digital Currencies
description: Learn Central Bank Digital Currencies in one minute.

hook.text: China's digital yuan lets the government track every transaction in real time. 260 million people already use it.

buildup.text: CBDCs are government-issued digital currencies — like cash, but electronic and programmable.

discovery.text: They could make monetary policy instant: stimulus payments arrive in seconds, not weeks.

twist.text: Programmable money could have expiration dates or spending restrictions. Governments decide how you spend.

climax.text: Over 130 countries are exploring CBDCs. The balance between efficiency and surveillance is the core tension.

punchline.text: Digital cash could be the most powerful financial tool or the most invasive.

quiz.question: What makes CBDCs different from cryptocurrency like Bitcoin?
options: CBDCs are issued and controlled by a central government
CBDCs have a fixed supply like Bitcoin

details.summary: Central bank digital currencies are government-issued digital money distinct from cryptocurrency. Unlike Bitcoin, CBDCs are centrally controlled and backed by the full faith of the issuing government. China's digital yuan and the Bahamas' Sand Dollar are early implementations.
details.whyItMatters: CBDCs could transform how money works by enabling instant free transfers, programmable money, and financial inclusion for the unbanked while raising serious concerns about government surveillance and financial privacy.
takeaways: CBDCs are government-backed digital currency, not decentralized crypto
China's digital yuan is the largest CBDC pilot with hundreds of millions of users
Privacy concerns arise from governments tracking every transaction digitally

faq.question: How are CBDCs different from regular digital banking?
faq.answer: Current digital money in bank accounts is actually commercial bank deposits, not direct central bank money. A CBDC would be a direct claim on the central bank, like digital cash. This eliminates bank intermediary risk but changes the role of commercial banks fundamentally.

faq.question: What are the main concerns about CBDCs?
faq.answer: Government surveillance of all transactions, the ability to program money with expiration dates or spending restrictions, potential disintermediation of commercial banks, and cybersecurity risks of centralizing an entire monetary system in digital infrastructure.
